items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1959-01-07
items.q: my cousin, first cousin was named Mac Boy

ctx.x: How did you get the name of T-Boy too?

How did you get the name of T-Boy? Well, I tell you, my cousin, first cousin was named Mac Boy. And his sister, they named his sister, Mac T-Girl. So, they named my sister, this one here, T-Girl. Then they named me T-Boy. That was nicknames, you know. T-Boy, T-Girl, Mac Boy, Mac T-Girl. That's how I got the name.
Does it mean anything? How? Does it mean anything? Is it tea? Is it tea you drink?

items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1959-12-23
items.q: Mack Murray took a lot of two-bar breaks... He was a great drummer.

ctx.x: They wouldn't even take a two-bar break?

Well, yeah. Well, a two-bar break. Yeah. I mean, you know. Mack Murray took a lot of two-bar breaks, but I can recall. Mack Murray used to drop the chain, blew the whistles, racket. He had a racket with a break on a racket. He had a lot of doodads. I mean, you see, he was a Mack Murray. He was a great drummer.
He had a big set then, with all his traps.

items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1959-01-07
items.q: We had a many good musicians, good drummers. Many good drummers. Mack Murray, Walter Brundy.

ctx.x: He used to play shows with Johnny Marl. That's right, yeah.

He played with him. We had a many good musicians, good drummers. Many good drummers. Mack Murray, Walter Brundy. Walter Brundy, Walter Brundy, Leon, he played clarinet. He was pretty fair. They had, they had, they had, Tick Chambers, he was a pretty good trumpet player too, Tick Chambers. Never hear a fella named Ned. Ned, yeah.
Was that his last name or first name? No, I don't remember.
